g.text: get components ready to be started
component is ready to be started
The graph only counts the component as in flight.
The main loop does not wait for it and returns to
activation is taken by a free worker
[the process PID cannot be entered into the map]
kill the process that was started (SIGKILL)
[the process has already exited when it is registered]
ready condition fulfilled, failed or ready timeout expired
The process could not be started, or its PID could not
be entered into the map. The attempt fails right away;
nothing is left running, so there is no cleanup.
[the ready condition is satisfied and the process did not exit unexpectedly]
The component is ready, no further attempt is made.
[the ready condition is satisfied, but supervision cannot be started]
The attempt fails and goes to the cleanup below, so a
supervised process never runs without supervision.
The ready timeout expired, the ready condition failed,
the process exited unexpectedly, or the activation was
cancelled. The attempt fails and goes to the cleanup below.
[cleanup: the attempt failed after the process was started]
wait for the termination of the process,
wait for the termination of the process,
activation failed with the result of the last attempt
next components ready to be started
Once the transition reports that nothing is left,
The graph moves to kAborting. The components still in
flight finish their current step and report back.
Components that are already running stay running.
The two queues are the only interaction between the threads: the graph never
touches a component directly and a worker never touches the graph. All graph
and transition state stays confined to the main loop thread.
Several components may be in flight at the same time; a single one is shown
